The `entire/*` local branches in euno-app are not project work. They are session

- Enabled per-repo via `.entire/settings.json` -> `{"enabled": true}`

- Shadow branches are named `entire/<HEAD-short-sha>-<suffix>` and get recreated
  when HEAD moves. A `git reset --hard` will make a new one appear.
- Commit subjects on these branches are raw session prompts, not commit
  messages, which is how to recognize them at a glance.

us.auth.entire.io is no longer valid, `entire doctor` shows stuck sessions, and
no `entire/*` branch has ever been pushed (origin holds only `main`). So it
collects locally and the data goes nowhere.

**Why:** these branches show up in every `git branch` listing and look like
abandoned work worth deleting. They are not, but they are also not currently
earning their keep.

**How to apply:** do not delete `entire/*` branches as part of a normal branch
cleanup. Either re-auth with `entire login` to use it, or `entire disable` +
`entire clean` to turn it off properly, which is the only way that also removes
the hooks. Deleting the branches by hand while it stays enabled just means it
recreates them. See [[worktree-cwd-hazard]] for the other repo-shape gotcha.

Search lay: [Image #4]") rather than commit messages.
